terms.definition: A type of control, which has a demonstrated effect, administered as a comparator to participants in a clinical trial.

codelists.ichDefinition: Terminology relevant to the data elements in section 1 of the ICH M11 protocol template.

terms.definition: An indication as to whether the clinical trial uses an adaptive trial design.
A narrative providing additional details about the duration of a participant's use of a trial intervention or their planned participation time in the trial.

terms.definition: An identifying designation assigned to a blinded individual within a clinical trial that corresponds with their function.
A characterisation or classification of the comparator against which the study intervention is evaluated.
An indication as to whether the clinical trial is testing a drug-device combination product.
An independent group of experts that has oversight over, and conducts periodic review of, specific trial activities.
A unique name that is globally recognised and public property, which identifies pharmaceutical substances or active pharmaceutical ingredients.
The technique used to assign trial participants to a trial intervention or trial arm.
The overall design configuration for assigning intervention to participants.
An indication as to whether the protocol is a master protocol.
The anticipated maximum age of the participants to be entered in a clinical trial.
The anticipated minimum age of the participants to be entered in a clinical trial.
Drug name that is not protected by a trademark, usually descriptive of its chemical structure, and sometimes a public name.
The planned number of intervention groups.
The planned number of participants to be entered in a clinical trial.
A committee that is different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned.
Description of any intervention assignment method that is different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned.
A description of the condition, disease or disorder that the clinical trial is intended to investigate or address.
A characterisation or classification of the trial population.

The target or maximum number of participants who have been randomly assigned to the trial intervention or enrolled in the trial.

terms.definition: A standardised representation of planned clinical trial activities including interventions (e.g., administering drug, surgery) and study administrative activities (e.g., obtaining informed consent, distributing clinical trial material and diaries, randomisation) as well as assessments.
A brief written record describing the trial schematic.
An indication as to whether the occurrence applies to a single or multiple trial sites.
An indication as to whether the trial is taking place in one or more countries.
An indication as to whether stratification is used as part of the randomisation process.
A characterisation or classification of the trial participant numbers as to whether the numbers reflect a target or maximum.
terms.preferredTerm: Trial Participation Number Target or Maximum Indicator

terms.ichPreferredTerm: total planned duration of trial intervention unit of time

terms.ichPreferredTerm: total planned duration of trial participation
terms.definition: The numeric value for the planned duration of trial participation.

The type of experimental design used to describe the level of awareness of the trial participants and/ or personnel as it relates to the respective intervention(s) or assessments being observed, received or administered.
A diagram that outlines the decision points (e.g. randomisation, response evaluation) that define the different paths a participant could take through the trial.
Those units of time that are routinely used to express the age of a person.

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Analyses Associated with the Exploratory Objective(s)
terms.definition: A description of the statistical model, hypothesis, and methods of analyses for each exploratory objective within the trial.

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Analyses of Demographics and Other Baseline Variables
terms.definition: A description of analyses relevant to variables at baseline, for example demographics, related to the trial.
terms.preferredTerm: Description of Trial Baseline Variable Analysis

terms.definition: A description of the set of participants whose data are to be included in the analyses.
terms.preferredTerm: Description of the Participants Included in Data Analysis

terms.definition: Careful thought or deliberation related to the planned conduct of statistical analyses within the context of the trial.

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Handling of Data in Relation to Primary Estimand(s)
terms.definition: A description of how data will be handled for the statistical analysis in line with the primary estimand.
terms.preferredTerm: Handling of Data in Relation to Primary Estimand(s)

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Handling of Data in Relation to Secondary Estimand(s)

terms.preferredTerm: Handling of Data in Relation to Secondary Estimand(s)

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Handling of Missing Data in Relation to Primary Estimand(s)

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Handling of Missing Data in Relation to Secondary Estimand(s)

terms.preferredTerm: Handling of Missing Data in Relation to Secondary Estimand(s)

terms.definition: A description of any analysis intended to compare treatment arms with respect to efficacy or safety at any time prior to the formal completion of a trial.
A description of the statistical adjustments needed to limit the probability of false positive findings in trials where there are multiple simultaneous hypotheses.
A description of the analyses that are different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned.
A description of the analyses of relevant safety variables, including adverse events of special interest.

A statistical calculation to determine the number of participants required for the primary analysis, which should be large enough to provide a reliable answer to the questions addressed and should be determined by the primary objective of the trial. If the sample size is determined on some other basis, then this should be made clear and justified.
A description of the series of analyses conducted to explore the robustness of inferences from the main estimator to deviations from its underlying modeling assumptions and limitations in the data.
A description of the statistical model, hypothesis, and methods of analyses for each objective within the trial.
A description of the analyses that are conducted in addition to the main and sensitivity analysis with the intent to provide additional insights into the understanding of the treatment effect.

A description of the key processes to ensure data integrity, traceability and security, in order to enable accurate collection, reporting, monitoring, transfer, retention, access and publication.

A description of how trial-related source records will be identified.
A description of the consent requirements for participants in the event of screen failure and rescreening.

terms.definition: A concise summary of the arrangements for participants insurance and indemnity as required by the applicable regulatory body.
A description of the obligations of the investigator with respect to maintaining and ensuring availability of the source records.
A description of the obligations of the investigator with respect to the trial.
A description of plans for detecting, reviewing, and reporting any deviations from the protocol.
Careful thought or deliberation related to the regulatory and ethical aspects of the trial.
The responsibilities of the sponsor and/or investigator following an unplanned early termination or suspension of the trial at an individual site.
terms.preferredTerm: Responsibilities Following Early Trial Site Closure

terms.definition: A description of how potential risks and critical to quality factors associated with the trial will be identified and handled.
A description of trial-related source records including the importance of source record maintenance and expectations for data traceability.
A description of the obligations of the sponsor with respect to the trial.

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Trial Monitor Expectations for Source Records

terms.preferredTerm: Trial Monitor Expectations for Source Records

The variable to be obtained for each patient that is required to address the clinical question. The specification of the variable might include whether the patient experiences an intercurrent event.
The exploratory reason for performing a study in terms of the scientific questions to be answered by the analysis of data collected during the study.
A description of the planned strategy to address intercurrent events.

Population level summary for the clinical endpoint of interest, which provides a basis for comparison between treatment conditions.
The principle reason for performing a study in terms of the scientific questions to be answered by the analysis of data collected during the study.
The secondary reason for performing a study in terms of the scientific questions to be answered by the analysis of data collected during the study.

The treatment condition of interest and, as appropriate, the alternative treatment condition to which comparison will be made (referred to as "treatment" through the remainder of this document). A description of the restrictions related to trial participant lifestyle such as diet, substance intake, and physical or other daily activities.
A description of the restrictions related to participant diet during the trial.

terms.definition: An activity restriction that is different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned.
A description of the restrictions related to participant physical activity during the trial.
The process of active consideration of participants for enrollment in a trial, for those potential participants who have failed a prior screening attempt.

terms.definition: The way in which the investigational trial intervention is dispensed, applied, or tendered to the trial participant.

terms.preferredTerm: Management of Investigational Trial Intervention Overdose

terms.definition: A description of the measures taken to ensure the blinding is maintained.
Description of any noninvestigational intervention that is different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned.

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Participant Assignment to Investigational Trial Intervention
terms.definition: The technique used to assign trial participants to a trial arm.

terms.definition: Concomitant therapy that is approved for use in the trial.

Physical characteristics of a drug product, (e.g., tablet, capsule, or solution) that contains a drug substance, generally-but not necessarily-in association with one or more other ingredients. (CDISC Glossary)
The way in which the investigational trial intervention is prepared for use or administration to the trial participant.
Concomitant therapy that is banned from use in the trial.

Path by which the pharmaceutical product is taken into or makes contact with the body.
An indication as to whether the investigational intervention is centrally or locally sourced.

terms.definition: Exploratory clinical trials, in a small number of participants, that are conducted early in Phase 1. The investigational trial intervention is administered at a low dose for a limited time. Early Phase 1 trials provide insights into a variety of parameters such as pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and other biomarkers. They involve limited human exposure, have no therapeutic or diagnostic intent, and are not intended to assess clinical tolerability.

Exploratory clinical trials that may be first-in-human, conducted in a small number of patients or healthy volunteers to evaluate clinical safety, tolerability, or therapeutic intent (pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics) of an investigational trial intervention.
A single clinical trial that combines elements of Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials, which may begin as a Phase 1 trial and transition into Phase 2 based upon predetermined criteria.

A single clinical trial that combines elements of Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3 trials, which may begin as a Phase 1 trial and transitions through Phase 2 and Phase 3 based upon predetermined criteria.
A single clinical trial that combines elements of Phase 1 and Phase 3 trials, which may begin as a Phase 1 trial and transition into Phase 3 based upon predetermined criteria.

Exploratory trials conducted to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the investigational trial intervention in patients with the disease or condition. Objectives may include, but are not limited to, clinical pharmacology, dose-ranging (dose-response, frequency of dosing), type of patients, or other characteristics of safety and efficacy.
A single clinical trial that combines elements of Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials, which may begin as a Phase 2 trial and transition into Phase 3 based upon predetermined criteria.

A single clinical trial that combines elements of Phase 2, Phase 3, and Phase 4 trials, which may begin as a Phase 2 trial and transitions through Phase 3 and Phase 4 based upon predetermined criteria.

Confirmatory trials conducted to demonstrate safety, efficacy and tolerability of the investigational trial intervention in patients with the disease or condition. Their objectives are to evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship and may provide substantial evidence for regulatory approval and product information.
A single clinical trial that combines elements of Phase 3 and Phase 4 trials, which may begin as a Phase 3 trial and transition into Phase 4 based upon predetermined criteria.

Post-approval (or post-marketing) trials conducted to further evaluate the safety and efficacy of an investigational trial intervention in its approved indication and may be conducted to address a regulatory requirement. These studies may explore use of the investigational trial intervention in the real-world setting of clinical practice and may also inform health economics and health technology assessments.

terms.definition: Any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation participant administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment.
Any concern about the safety, quality, and/or performance of a trial-related drug-device combination.
Any event that occurs when the participant is lactating.

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Not Reportable Adverse Event of Special Interest
terms.definition: An adverse event of special interest (serious or non-serious) is one of scientific and medical concern specific to the sponsor's product or program, for which ongoing monitoring and rapid communication by the investigator to the sponsor could be appropriate, and which is deemed to be not reportable to the appropriate regulatory authority.
terms.preferredTerm: Not Reportable Adverse Event of Special Interest

terms.definition: Different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned.
Any event that occurs when the participant is in the stages of recovery post pregnancy and birth event.
Any event that occurs when the participant or participant's partner becomes pregnant or is pregnant.

terms.ichPreferredTerm: Reportable Adverse Event of Special Interest
terms.definition: An adverse event of special interest (serious or non-serious) is one of scientific and medical concern specific to the sponsor's product or program, for which ongoing monitoring and rapid communication by the investigator to the sponsor could be appropriate, and which is deemed to be reportable to the appropriate regulatory authority.
terms.preferredTerm: Reportable Adverse Event of Special Interest

terms.definition: Any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or any other medically significant event that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but may jeopardise the patient or may require intervention to prevent one of the other outcomes listed in the definition.
Any concern about the safety and/or quality of any trial-related interventions.
